citations.quote: ## 8.1.1. Study 1 (Chae et al. 2019)

The effectiveness of CERIANNA for detecting ER-positive non-primary breast cancer lesions was evaluated based on published study reports of fluoroestradiol F 18. Study 1 (NCT01986569) enrolled 90 women (median age 55 years, 39% premenopausal) with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer.
Phase 3, prospective, non-randomized, single-center cohort study.

design.text: Phase 3, prospective, non-randomized, single-center cohort study with blinded, central independent image interpretation.

citations.quote: Phase 3, prospective, non-randomized, single-center cohort study.
Three central, independent nuclear medicine physicians were blinded to patient medical records, including pathology results.

population.text: Women with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer with first known or suspected recurrence of treated breast cancer or stage IV metastatic breast cancer; all 90 participants were Korean women.

citations.quote: Study 1 (NCT01986569) enrolled 90 women (median age 55 years, 39% premenopausal) with histologically confirmed invasive breast cancer.
The patients had first known or suspected recurrence of treated breast cancer or stage IV metastatic breast cancer.
All 90 participants in Study 1 (Chae et al. 2019) were Korean women.

endpoint.text: Agreement between qualitative FES scan interpretation and pathologically based ER status (positive and negative percent agreement, PPA/NPA).

citations.quote: The primary objective was to show agreement between qualitative FES scan interpretation and pathologically based ER status.

n.text: 90 patients completed the FES PET scan; 85 patients included in the efficacy analysis (47 ER-positive, 38 ER-negative).

citations.quote: Of the 85 patients included in the efficacy analysis, 47 (55%) were ER-positive (Allred score 3 to 8) and 38 (45%) ER-negative (Allred score 0 to 2).
Subjects completed FES PET (n)	90

result.text: FES scan positive in 36 of 47 ER-positive patients (PPA 76.6%); all 38 ER-negative patients had negative FES PET (NPA 100%); positive predictive agreement 100%, negative predictive agreement 77.6%.

citations.quote: FES scan was positive in 36 of 47 ER-positive patients, yielding a PPA of 76.6%. All 38 ER-negative patients had negative FES PET, yielding an NPA of 100%. With the same 2x2 tabulation data analyzed based on proportion of positive and negative FES scans, positive predictive agreement was 100% and negative predictive agreement was 77.6%.

indication.text: CERIANNA is indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) imaging for the detection of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive lesions as an adjunct to biopsy in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer.

citations.quote: CERIANNA is indicated for use with positron emission tomography (PET) imaging for the detection of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive lesions as an adjunct to biopsy in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer.

target_moa.text: Fluoroestradiol F 18 is a fluorinated synthetic derivative of 17β-estradiol that binds with competitive high affinity to estrogen receptors (ER-α and ER-β); its mechanism of action is via ER binding, and PET imaging detects its uptake in ER-positive tissue.

citations.quote: FES is a fluorinated synthetic derivative of the endogenous sex steroid, 17\beta-estradiol (estradiol or ES). Binding studies conducted with FES demonstrate competitive, high-affinity binding to estrogen receptors alpha and beta (ER-\alpha and ER-\beta), and moderate affinity to the plasma proteins sex-hormone binding globulin (SHBG), and \alpha-fetoprotein (\alpha FP).
The mechanism of action of FES is via ER binding.
CERIANNA is radiolabeled with F 18, a cyclotron produced radionuclide that decays by positron emission to stable oxygen 18 with a half-life of 109.8 minutes.

key_safety.text: Safety evaluated in published studies of 1207 patients; reported adverse reactions (each occurring at a rate <1%) were injection-site pain and dysgeusia. In Study 1, the most common adverse event was procedural pain in 9 (10%) of 90 patients; no serious adverse events occurred.

citations.quote: The safety of CERIANNA was evaluated from published clinical studies of 1207 patients with breast cancer receiving at least one fluoroestradiol F 18 administration. The following adverse reactions occurred at a rate < 1%:

- *General disorders*: injection-site pain
- *Neurological and gastrointestinal disorders*: dysgeusia

The most common adverse event was procedural pain in nine (10%) of 90 patients injected with FES. No adverse events occurred that were related to the study drug except injection site pain in one (1%) patient. No serious adverse events occurred during the study and there were no treatment-related deaths

detail.text: The review team recommended approval of this NDA and the office director concurred; no prior CRL is described.

citations.quote: The review team finds that the benefit-risk of Cerianna is favorable for detection of estrogen receptor (ER)-positive lesions as an adjunct to biopsy in patients with recurrent or metastatic breast cancer. Applicant has agreed to major recommended labeling revisions, and the review team therefore recommends approval of this NDA.
